description.narrative: The explosion at the Port of Beirut at 6:10pm on Tuesday 4th August 2020 caused extensive damage, loss of life and has impacted hundreds of thousands of people in Beirut. As of 25th September, over 190 people are reported to have died, with more than 6,500 people injured. The Government of Lebanon estimates that around 300,000 people were made homeless following the Beirut Port explosion and up to 40,000 buildings sustained damage. The explosion occurred while Lebanon faces a deep economic and political crisis, and rising COVID-19 cases. Protests against the Lebanese government have been taking place for months in Beirut prompting the Government to step down on 10 August 2020. Poverty has risen in recent months; 2.7 million residents are now poor and 1.1. million are extremely poor. The Lebanese Red Cross immediately mobilized its teams and assets to respond to the blast. They have launched a one-year Response Plan appealing for $125 million to respond to the needs of those affected by the multiple overlapping shocks faced by many in Lebanon during 2020.

Please see attached the GAD addendum 1 and supporting documentation including the bank details for the DF allocation to the DMU of LRC in response to the Beirut explosion. On 4 August a large explosion occurred in the port of Beirut, killing over 170 people and injuring an estimated 6,000. A number of sectors of Greater Beirut have been significantly affected by the blast - businesses and infrastructure have been destroyed or damaged, and up to 300,000 people are thought to have lost their homes. The Disaster Management Sector at the Lebanese Red Cross will be providing a several tier response with both direct response to the blast in coordination with Blood Transfusion services and long-term objectives to improve the living conditions of the affected population through the provision of shelters and basic needs to 10,000 families in a three months response through 3 phases: Phase one: Conduct a Post Disaster Assessment (PDA) followed by a door-to-door emergency needs assessment and Damage Assessment and Needs Analysis (DANA) accompanied with distribution of ready-made meals and water Phase two: Provision of food parcels, hygiene kits and shelter-improvement kits for eligible families affected by the explosion. Phase three: Facilitation of a long-term suitable shelter solution through the modalities seen as fit (e.g. Cash and Shelter equipment)
•Direct Response in Coordination with BTS: Activating hotlines for receiving shelter requests, filing for Restoring Family Links (RFL) cases. •Supporting Blood Transfusion Services with logistic services, management of blood donation. •Processing, and transportation of blood units to hospitals throughout the emergency response. •Supporting the expansion, installation, and maintenance of two LRC field operation points. •Provision of logistical support for LRC staff and volunteers throughout the operation Due to sending these original funds to the wrong account, this was reimbursed back to the BRC.
